facts.statement: Fernando Escaso and colleagues formally named Eousdryosaurus in 2014, following a brief description in 2000.
facts.quote: Eousdryosaurus was named in 2014 by Fernando Escaso and colleagues, after having been described briefly in 2000.

facts.statement: The fossils were discovered in late Kimmeridgian-age sandstone (approximately 152 million years old) in the Lourinhã Formation, Portugal.
facts.quote: These bones were discovered in sandstone of the late Kimmeridgian-age (late Jurassic, approximately 152 million years old) Praia da Amoreira-Porto Novo Member of the Lourinhã Formation in Porto das Barcas, Lourinhã, Portugal.

facts.statement: The genus name references the animal being a relative of Dryosaurus located on the east side of the Atlantic Ocean.
facts.quote: The genus name is a reference to Eousdryosaurus being a relative of Dryosaurus on the east side of the Atlantic Ocean.

facts.statement: The species name nanohallucis means "small hallux," referring to the small size of the big toe.
facts.quote: E. nanohallucis, meaning "small hallux", in reference to the small size of that toe.

facts.statement: The only known individual was a small dryosaurid estimated at 1.6 meters in length, comparable to immature Dryosaurus and Dysalotosaurus.
facts.quote: The only known individual of Eousdryosaurus was a small dryosaurid, estimated at 1.6 m in length, comparable to immature individuals of Dryosaurus and Dysalotosaurus.

facts.statement: The foot is unique among ornithopods because the first digit (hallux) includes only a single phalanx bone, whereas most basal ornithopods had two and most derived ones lost it entirely.
facts.quote: The foot is unique among ornithopods in that the first digit (the hallux or big toe) includes a single phalanx bone; most basal ornithopods had two phalanges, and most derived ornithopods, including hadrosaurs ("duckbills"), lost this digit.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis by Escaso et al. placed Eousdryosaurus as a basal dryosaurid within the Dryomorpha, a group of small bipedal herbivores near the base of Iguanodontia.
facts.quote: Escaso et al. performed a phylogenetic analysis and found Eousdryosaurus to be a basal dryosaurid within the Dryomorpha, a type of small bipedal herbivore near the base of Iguanodontia.

facts.statement: Dieudonné et al. (2020) suggested Eousdryosaurus is a sister taxon to the Elasmaria, contrasting with other studies.
facts.quote: On the other hand, Dieudonné et al. (2020) found Eousdryosaurus to be a sister taxon to the Elasmaria.

facts.statement: Rotatori et al. (2024) found support for a dryosaurid position for Eousdryosaurus, contrasting with the suggestions of Dieudonné et al. (2020).
facts.quote: In their 2024 description of the contemporary Hesperonyx, Rotatori et al. found support for a dryosaurid position of Eousdryosaurus in both their parsimony and Bayesian analyses, contrasting with the suggestions of Dieudonné et al. (2020).

facts.statement: Eousdryosaurus nanohallucis lived during the late Jurassic, approximately 152 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: Eousdryosaurus nanohallucis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Eousdryosaurus ("Dryosaurus del este") de dinosaurio ornitópodo driosáurido que vivió a finales del período jurásico, hace aproximadamente 152 millones de años en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: The foot claw formula is 1-3-4-5-0, with the first toe claw being extremely reduced, flattened vertically, elongated, and pointed.
facts.quote: La fórmula para las uñas de los pies es 1-3-4-5-0, con la garra del primer dedo extremadamente reducida, aplanada verticalmente, alargada y puntiaguda.

facts.statement: This represents a case of parallel evolution where a foot digit was lost from the first toe, leaving a very small, bone-tip-like remnant.
facts.quote: Este sería un caso de evolución paralela. Una pata del dedo del pie se perdió así desde el primer dedo del pie. La platija restante es muy pequeña, no más que una punta de hueso sin forma.

facts.statement: In 1999, an amateur paleontologist found the skeleton of a small euornithopod in Porto das Barcas, Lourinhã.
facts.quote: En 1999, en Porto das Barcas, Lourinhã, un paleontólogo aficionado, encontró el esqueleto de un pequeño euornitópodo.

facts.statement: The fossil was provisionally described in 2000 and nicknamed "Manuelino".
facts.quote: Este fue descrito provisionalmente en 2000 y apodado "Manuelino".

facts.statement: Eousdryosaurus is based on the holotype SHN(JJS)-170, housed in the Sociedade de Historia Natural in Torres Vedras, Portugal.
facts.quote: Eousdryosaurus está basado en el holotipo SHN(JJS)-170, alojado en la Sociedade de Historia Natural en Torres Vedras, Portugal.

facts.statement: The genus name references Eousdryosaurus being a relative of Dryosaurus that lived on the east side of the Atlantic Ocean.
facts.quote: El nombre del género es una referencia a que Eousdryosaurus era un pariente de Dryosaurus que vivía del lado este del océano Atlántico.

facts.statement: The foot is unique among ornithopods because its first digit (hallux) includes only a single phalanx, while many basal ornithopods had two and advanced ones lost it entirely.
facts.quote: El pie es único entre los ornitópodos ya que su primer dígito o hallux solo incluye una única falange, muchos ornitópodos basales tenían dos falanges, y los ornitópodos más avanzados, incluyendo a los hadrosáuridos perdieron ese dígito.

facts.statement: The time range for Eousdryosaurus is from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian (152.21 to 145.06 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (152.21 to 145.06 million years ago)
